tidycreel and the survey Package: A Side-by-Side Guide

Source: vignettes/survey-tidycreel.Rmd
survey-tidycreel.Rmd

For a design with instantaneous counts and access interviews, tidycreel’s effort, catch rate and total catch are built from survey package calls: svytotal() for effort, svyratio() for the rate, and svyby() to do each stratum separately. This page reproduces each of those three numbers with survey directly, so the two can be read side by side.

It covers that one design. Other designs add steps of their own (bus-route inclusion probabilities, aerial calibration, camera ratios), described on their own pages; the reasoning behind each choice here is in the Explanation pages vignette("effort-pipeline") and vignette("catch-pipeline").

The data

The season from vignette("tidycreel"): 120 days in two strata, 36 of them sampled, one instantaneous count on each sampled day, and access interviews.

library(tidycreel)
library(survey)

table(example_season_calendar$day_type) # days in the season, N_h
#> 
#> weekday weekend 
#>      86      34
table(example_season_counts$day_type) # days sampled, n_h
#> 
#> weekday weekend 
#>      28       8
head(example_season_counts, 3)
#>         date day_type total_anglers daylight_hours
#> 1 2024-05-06  weekday             5             14
#> 2 2024-05-07  weekday             5             14
#> 3 2024-05-09  weekday             9             14
head(example_season_interviews, 3)
#>         date day_type interview_id trip_status hours_fished n_anglers
#> 1 2024-05-06  weekday            1  incomplete         1.78         2
#> 2 2024-05-06  weekday            2  incomplete         1.82         1
#> 3 2024-05-06  weekday            3    complete         4.66         3
#>   catch_total catch_kept
#> 1           0          0
#> 2           3          1
#> 3           1          0

The tidycreel version, run once and used for comparison below:

design <- creel_design(example_season_calendar, date = date, strata = day_type)
design <- add_counts(design, example_season_counts,
  count_col = total_anglers,
  period_length_col = daylight_hours
)
design <- add_interviews(design, example_season_interviews,
  catch = catch_total,
  effort = hours_fished,
  trip_status = trip_status,
  n_anglers = n_anglers
)

effort <- estimate_effort(design, target = "period_total")
rate <- estimate_catch_rate(design)
total <- estimate_total_catch(design, target = "period_total")

Effort: svytotal()

A day’s effort is its count times the length of the period the count was randomised within: anglers present × hours open, in angler-hours. The days are a stratified sample, and each sampled day stands for Nh/nhN_h / n_h days of its stratum:

counts <- example_season_counts
counts$angler_hours <- counts$total_anglers * counts$daylight_hours

N_h <- table(example_season_calendar$day_type)
n_h <- table(counts$day_type)
counts$w <- as.numeric(N_h[counts$day_type] / n_h[counts$day_type])

count_design <- svydesign(
  ids = ~1, strata = ~day_type, weights = ~w, data = counts
)
svytotal(~angler_hours, count_design)
#>               total     SE
#> angler_hours 9994.5 1286.3

effort$estimates
#> # A tibble: 1 × 7
#>   estimate    se se_between se_within ci_lower ci_upper     n
#>      <dbl> <dbl>      <dbl>     <dbl>    <dbl>    <dbl> <int>
#> 1    9994. 1286.      1286.         0    7380.   12609.    36
effort$unit
#> [1] "angler-hours"

The estimate and standard error are the same. tidycreel’s confidence interval uses a tt quantile on the design’s degrees of freedom, 36 days less 2 strata; confint() uses the normal quantile unless it is given them:

confint(svytotal(~angler_hours, count_design), df = degf(count_design))
#>                 2.5 %  97.5 %
#> angler_hours 7380.401 12608.6

No finite-population correction

The design above has no finite-population correction (FPC). Survey texts would usually add one, because days are drawn without replacement:

counts$fpc <- as.numeric(N_h[counts$day_type])
svytotal(~angler_hours, svydesign(
  ids = ~1, strata = ~day_type, fpc = ~fpc, data = counts
))
#>               total     SE
#> angler_hours 9994.5 1078.6

The standard error falls from about 1,286 to 1,079. tidycreel leaves the correction out when a day has one count. The between-day variance then also carries the variation from when in the day the count fell, and sampling more days does not remove that part. With two or more counts on every sampled day of a stratum, tidycreel estimates the within-day part separately and applies the correction to the between-day part. The reasoning is in vignette("effort-pipeline"); up to tidycreel 8.0.0 the correction was always applied (#505).

Catch rate: svyratio()

The rate comes from complete trips. Its denominator is angler-hours, each party’s hours times its number of anglers. The interviews are stratified by day type and weighted equally:

trips <- subset(example_season_interviews, trip_status == "complete")
trips$angler_hours <- trips$hours_fished * trips$n_anglers

trip_design <- svydesign(
  ids = ~1, strata = ~day_type, weights = ~1, data = trips
)
svyratio(~catch_total, ~angler_hours, trip_design)
#> Ratio estimator: svyratio.survey.design2(~catch_total, ~angler_hours, trip_design)
#> Ratios=
#>             angler_hours
#> catch_total    0.2207121
#> SEs=
#>             angler_hours
#> catch_total   0.04148304

rate$estimates
#> # A tibble: 1 × 5
#>   estimate     se ci_lower ci_upper     n
#>      <dbl>  <dbl>    <dbl>    <dbl> <int>
#> 1    0.221 0.0415    0.139    0.302   172
rate$unit
#> [1] "fish/angler-hour"

This is the ratio of means (total catch over total effort), the estimator for access interviews; vignette("estimator-choice") covers when tidycreel uses the mean of ratios instead. Without n_anglers, the denominator would be party hours and the rate would be per party-hour, about 0.37 here instead of 0.22. The two are different quantities, and tidycreel reports which one it computed in unit.

Total catch: svyby() and a product variance

The total is not season effort times the season rate. It is built within each stratum and the strata are then added, Ĉ=∑hÊhR̂h\hat{C} = \sum_h \hat{E}_h \hat{R}_h, so that each stratum’s rate is weighted by that stratum’s effort:

E <- svyby(~angler_hours, ~day_type, count_design, svytotal)
R <- svyby(~catch_total, ~day_type, trip_design, svyratio,
  denominator = ~angler_hours
)
E
#>         day_type angler_hours       se
#> weekday  weekday       7912.0 1062.602
#> weekend  weekend       2082.5  724.896
R
#>         day_type catch_total/angler_hours se.catch_total/angler_hours
#> weekday  weekday                0.2081839                  0.04530168
#> weekend  weekend                0.2801120                  0.10241615

e <- coef(E)
r <- coef(R)
se_e <- SE(E)
se_r <- SE(R)

sum(e * r)
#> [1] 2230.484
sqrt(sum(e^2 * se_r^2 + r^2 * se_e^2 - se_e^2 * se_r^2))
#> [1] 506.2577

total$estimates
#> # A tibble: 1 × 5
#>   estimate    se ci_lower ci_upper     n
#>      <dbl> <dbl>    <dbl>    <dbl> <int>
#> 1    2230.  506.    1231.    3230.   172
total$unit
#> [1] "fish"

The variance of each stratum’s product is Goodman’s unbiased estimator: the two delta-method terms minus the product of the two variances. The familiar two-term delta method is product_variance = "first_order". Both assume the effort and rate errors are independent; vignette("catch-pipeline") derives the formula and discusses that assumption.

Mapping table

Step survey package tidycreel
Day’s effort count × period length add_counts(count_col =, period_length_col =)
Count design svydesign(ids = ~1, strata = ~day_type, weights = ~N_h/n_h), no fpc with one count a day creel_design() + add_counts()
Effort svytotal(~angler_hours, ...) estimate_effort(target = "period_total")
Interview design complete trips; svydesign(ids = ~1, strata = ~day_type, weights = ~1) add_interviews()
Catch rate svyratio(~catch, ~angler_hours, ...) estimate_catch_rate()
Total catch svyby() per stratum; ∑hÊhR̂h\sum_h \hat{E}_h \hat{R}_h; Goodman variance estimate_total_catch(target = "period_total")
Confidence interval effort and total catch: confint(..., df = degf(design)); catch rate: confint(...), the normal interval ci_lower, ci_upper

What tidycreel adds on top of these calls is the bookkeeping: the unit of each result, the strata a total must be built within, the refusals when the data cannot support an estimate (vignette("refusals-and-na")), and the bootstrap and jackknife variance methods (vignette("replicate-designs")).

The internal design object

as_creel_svydesign() returns the count design tidycreel built, for use with other survey functions. It is the design over the sampled days with every weight 1, not the season design above, and its count column now holds each day’s count × period in angler-hours, under the column’s original name:

internal <- as_creel_svydesign(design)
head(internal$variables[, c("date", "day_type", "total_anglers")], 3)
#>         date day_type total_anglers
#> 1 2024-05-06  weekday            70
#> 2 2024-05-07  weekday            70
#> 3 2024-05-09  weekday           126
svytotal(~total_anglers, internal)
#>               total     SE
#> total_anglers  3066 385.72

That total is effort over the 36 sampled days. estimate_effort() expands it to the season, and is the way to get the season total.
